requirements.requirement: Forward node2 messages from the inventory application to a centralized collector on node1.
requirements.summary: node2 was configured to forward programname=inventory over TCP to node1 with a persistent queue. Direct tests show an established connection and inventory-tagged messages arriving on node1; an unrelated-app test was excluded.

requirements.requirement: Persist received inventory messages on node1 at /var/log/inventory/node2.log.
requirements.summary: The requested file contains multiple messages received from node2, has restrictive mode 0640, and retained its earlier contents through node1's restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep log flow working after either node1 or node2 restarts.
requirements.summary: Both restart transitions were directly exercised. For node1, a healthy pre-restart collector and existing data were observed, restart was acknowledged, the boot ID changed, rsyslog and TCP/514 recovered, existing data remained, and a message submitted during the outage arrived afterward. For node2, a healthy forwarding connection was observed, restart was acknowledged, the boot ID changed, rsyslog and its TCP connection recovered, and a new post-restart message reached node1. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate both restarts.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied with direct end-to-end and restart-transition evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is substantively complete for both managed nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered rsyslog service, and recovered end-to-end log behavior.
limitations: End-to-end traffic was generated with logger using the inventory program tag rather than observed from a distinct long-running inventory application process; discovery evidence indicated no such application artifacts were present.
The generic failed-service lifecycle probe is unsupported on these Alpine/OpenRC nodes, although direct rc-service checks show rsyslog healthy before and after both restarts.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Package installation, rsyslog configuration, replacement of BusyBox syslog, service enablement, test-message generation, and restarts all had clear roles in implementation or bounded verification. The initially failed receiver-configuration command still created the required log directory and was immediately completed by the corrected command, so it did not leave unrelated residue. Temporary-file inventories and package-health observations were unchanged, and the new TCP/514 listener is required by the collector role.
